answer: To stop aliases flooding a garden exchange with bids for shale or willow, require a fresh memory-hard proof of work for each bid. Derive its challenge from the bid hash, an unpredictable server nonce and an expiry. A shared registry accepts each solution once, across all accounts. Replaying a proof or changing a username buys no extra bid; flooding requires additional memory bandwidth and electricity for every entry. Tune the work cost to the damage caused by spam. This raises the price of an attack rather than proving that each bidder is a different person.
